title: Federal Schedule II dispensing rests on a signed written prescription except in the paragraph (d) emergency
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.11(a) a pharmacist may dispense directly a controlled substance listed in Schedule II that is a prescription drug as determined under section 503 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 353(b)) ONLY PURSUANT TO A WRITTEN PRESCRIPTION SIGNED BY THE PRACTITIONER, EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN PARAGRAPH (d) of that section, which permits dispensing upon oral authorization in an emergency situation. A paper prescription for a Schedule II controlled substance may be transmitted by the practitioner or the practitioner's agent to a pharmacy via facsimile equipment, PROVIDED THAT THE ORIGINAL MANUALLY SIGNED PRESCRIPTION IS PRESENTED TO THE PHARMACIST FOR REVIEW PRIOR TO THE ACTUAL DISPENSING of the controlled substance, except as noted in paragraphs (e), (f) and (g). The original prescription shall be maintained in accordance with 21 CFR 1304.04(h).
exam_relevance: Tests that federal law gives a Schedule II drug no oral route outside the paragraph (d) emergency exception, and that outside the settings named in paragraphs (e) through (g) a faxed Schedule II prescription does not stand in for the original manually signed prescription.

authority.name: Requirement of prescription for a Schedule II controlled substance

exceptions: Paragraph (d) permits a pharmacist to dispense a Schedule II controlled substance upon the oral authorization of a prescribing individual practitioner in an emergency situation as defined in 21 CFR 290.10.
Paragraphs (e), (f) and (g) name the settings in which a facsimile of a Schedule II prescription serves as the original written prescription.
common_confusions: Treating an oral Schedule II authorization as acceptable outside the paragraph (d) emergency situation.

Treating a faxed Schedule II prescription as the original outside the settings in paragraphs (e) through (g), when paragraph (a) requires the original manually signed prescription to be presented for review before the actual dispensing.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1306.11(a), with paragraphs (d) through (g) read alongside it, read on 2026-09-11 in the current eCFR section page for 21 CFR 1306.11, shown as up to date as of 9/09/2026. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
